flows.title: POST /api/v1/catalog/products – create product
flows.summary: A minimal-API endpoint sends CreateProductCommand through Mediator. Permission and idempotency run as endpoint metadata/filters, FluentValidation runs as a pipeline behavior, and the handler checks brand, category, SKU and slug before saving. SaveChanges triggers an audit interceptor and then publishes ProductCreatedDomainEvent.
flows.plain_summary: A user adds a product by sending POST /products. The Permission check confirms they are allowed, and the Idempotency filter makes sure a repeated request is not processed twice. mediator.Send passes the request on; ValidationBehavior uses CreateProductCommandValidator to check the details are complete, then CreateProductCommandHandler takes over. It asks Brand exists? and Category exists?, builds the product with Product.Create, and checks SKU taken? and Slug taken? so that no duplicate is created. SaveChangesAsync stores the product, the Auditable interceptor records who changed it, DomainEventsInterceptor announces the new product and CatalogEventHandlers reacts to that announcement. The user then receives 200 OK + product id. If any check fails along the way, GlobalExceptionHandler turns the problem into a clear error message for the user.

nodes.label: POST /products
nodes.description: Mapped on the catalog group (api/v{version}/catalog, RequireAuthorization). Declares the Products.Create permission and idempotency filter, then sends the command to Mediator.

nodes.label: Permission check
nodes.description: UseAuthorization runs the RequiredPermission policy, which reads the endpoint's RequiredPermissionAttribute metadata. Missing permission yields 403, no token 401.
nodes.note: Policy wiring is in JwtAuthenticationExtensions (default and fallback policy); the handler body was not traced line by line.

nodes.label: Idempotency filter
nodes.description: Opt-in via the Idempotency-Key header. Without it the request passes straight through. With it, a cached response is replayed, concurrent duplicates are rejected, and the first response is stored.

nodes.label: mediator.Send
nodes.description: Dispatches the command to the pipeline behaviors and then the handler.

nodes.label: ValidationBehavior
nodes.description: Pipeline behavior registered open-generic in Web/Extensions.cs. Runs every IValidator<CreateProductCommand> and throws ValidationException on any failure.

nodes.label: CreateProductCommandValidator
nodes.description: Rules: Sku required and max 64, Name required and max 200, brand and category ids non-empty, price and stock >= 0, currency exactly 3 chars.

nodes.label: CreateProductCommandHandler
nodes.description: Orchestrates the existence checks, builds the aggregate, checks SKU and slug uniqueness and saves.

nodes.label: Product.Create
nodes.description: Domain factory: guards, trims, upper-cases the SKU, builds the slug from the name, generates a Guid v7 id and queues ProductCreatedDomainEvent.

nodes.label: SKU taken?
nodes.description: Checks the normalized SKU. Done after Create so the comparison uses the same upper-cased value.

nodes.label: Slug taken?
nodes.description: Checks the generated slug, so two different names that slugify the same collide.

nodes.label: SaveChangesAsync
nodes.description: Adds the product to CatalogDbContext and commits. Returns the new product id.

nodes.label: Auditable interceptor
nodes.description: SavingChangesAsync hook stamping audit fields before the write.
nodes.note: Registered as an ISaveChangesInterceptor in PersistenceExtensions; stamped fields not read in detail.

nodes.label: DomainEventsInterceptor
nodes.description: After the commit, collects pending domain events from tracked entities and publishes each through Mediator. Handler failures are logged, never rethrown.

nodes.label: CatalogEventHandlers
nodes.description: Handles ProductCreatedDomainEvent. Currently only writes an information log line.

nodes.label: 200 OK + product id
nodes.description: Results.Ok wraps the Guid. With an Idempotency-Key the response is also cached for replay.

nodes.label: GlobalExceptionHandler
nodes.description: Registered via UseExceptionHandler. Maps ValidationException to 400, CustomException to its own status (404 not found, 409 conflict) and anything else to 500, as ProblemDetails.

notes: BuildingBlocks/Web/Mediator/Extensions.cs has EnableMediator, which also registers ValidationBehavior, but nothing calls it. Only Web/Extensions.cs:207 takes effect.
MediatorTracingBehavior is registered only when OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled, so a trace span may wrap the pipeline.
SKU and slug uniqueness are check-then-insert, so two concurrent creates can both pass. Only a database unique index would catch the race (not verified).
Domain event handler failures are swallowed after the commit, so there is no guaranteed delivery.
